newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields largely flat, crown softer.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields largely flat, crown softer.

text.p: Swedish bond yields were little changed at midday on Monday with the long end edging lower and the short end higher.

The crown was hurt early on by a news agency report saying Finance Minister Erik Asbrink had raised the spectre of devaluation but he was merely discussing monetary policy mechanisms available to countries outside EMU, he clarified.
He later denied the possibility of devaluing was a reason for staying outside the economic and monetary union (EMU).
The crown was changing hands at 4.5150 against the mark compared to 4.4910 late on Friday.
The six-month T-bill rate rose one basis point to 4.23 percent and the ten-year bond yield fell one basis point to 6.95 percent, underperforming international trends.
"Swedish yields are not falling by as much (as international yields) because of a softer crown," one dealer said.
He also said the focus will be on further movements in the U.S. following the sharp fall in yields on Friday.
Market players will also eye further developments at the Ecofin meeting in Luxembourg.
